records.summary: This is a tiny river ripple, not a dramatic plunge. The meaningful experience is the public riverside day-use park and its rustic path. This establishes a legitimate park-level place to walk, but the township does not certify exact waterfall naming/point geometry or current site conditions.

records.name: Au Train Falls
records.title: Au Train Falls: EGLE emergency dam order and unverified visitor access
records.summary: Investigated November 3, 2026: Michigan EGLE issued a June 2, 2026 emergency dam-safety order (#MI00152), citing serious structural deficiencies and ordering continued drawdown and a remediation/permit program. Michigan DNR reported March 2026 that the former hydropower campground and boat launch were no longer used after the 2025 land sale and lack of a new owner agreement; those facilities must not be mistaken for the two historic waterfall parking areas. FERC's December 29, 2025 FINAL termination order controls the federal license date and documents the split in project land ownership. Older Munising tourist directions point to two Power Dam Road lots but no current owner permission to park or use either trail. A June 2026 visitor reported No Trespassing at the upper lot, unverified by an official closure notice. Do not claim both falls closed; equally, do not recommend parking or entering gated utility facilities.
records.guidance: DECISION: NOT CLEARED FOR A PUBLIC WATERFALL TRIP. Verify current signed owner authorization for the exact upper or lower visitor lot, corresponding footpath and gates, plus EGLE/owner restrictions before travel. A June 2026 emergency dam order is not itself an order closing every falls trail. Do not drive to GIS #192, use old gated gravel roads, cross no-trespassing signs, approach dam works, wade near powerhouse outlets or infer safe flow from old photos.
records.reviewLimitations: FERC's December 29, 2025 FINAL termination order supersedes 2025 proposed surrender reporting. EGLE's June 2, 2026 owner-responsibility letter erroneously refers to November 29, 2025 as termination date: use FERC's signed final order. EGLE documents UP Hydro LLC ownership of dam embankment/levee parcels, while FERC documents the D. Charles Trust purchase of powerhouse/buffer project parcels. Neither supplies the cadastral visitor corridor for both falls. The March DNR campground/boat-launch nonuse is distinct from either waterfall lot unless mapped. June 2026 visitor 'No Trespassing' observation is anecdotal and cannot become an official full-site closure claim. No post-June order resolution, owner visitor approval, 2026 permit outcome or same-day restrictions independently verified.
records.nextEvidence: Obtain written present owner permission or a current official map for BOTH separate falls approaches with specific lot/trail parcels; verify gate/no-trespass signs and whether lower access remains legal. Check EGLE for emergency-order modification/termination and current construction, drawdown and safety buffers, including post July 2 and Aug 31 2026 filing status. Ask township/DNR whether a public access agreement was restored; campground/boat launch are not synonyms for falls parking.

records.name: Peavy Falls (dam and historic ledges)
records.title: Peavy Falls (dam and historic ledges): source and visitor access review
records.summary: The name survives, but hydroelectric engineering changed what a visitor might see. Neither a nearby fishing area nor a power-station flow number guarantees a visible natural waterfall. Michigan GIS #9 locates Peavy Falls on the Michigamme River at 45.990797,-88.209553. We Energies identifies a Peavy Falls hydroelectric plant built in 1943. The World Waterfall Database rates the natural feature unconfirmed, and explains that the original upper drop is diverted by the dam while water can reach a lower ledge through a spillway only when operations allow. This is specialist interpretation, not a verified present-day spill schedule or height survey.
records.guidance: Historic natural falls transformed by hydropower. No verified legal public viewing trail or direct falls-flow sensor; do not create a driving route to GIS #9 or a live waterfall-going-now verdict.
records.reviewLimitations: Geographic points, project-wide recreation facilities and hydroelectric telemetry do not establish an approved arrival, a signed walking route or live flow over a natural ledge.
records.nextEvidence: Acquire the current FERC/project recreation site map and precise legally accessible Peavy Falls viewing areas, if any; separate powerhouse/turbine total discharge, spillway release and bypassed natural ledges. Confirm road and shore permissions before any guide promotion.
